t: The Signature Bench Beam: Case-Tuned Flood
title: The Signature Bench Beam: Case-Tuned Flood
description: The Signature Bench Beam is Justin Addam Higgins' original headlamp: a fixed flood beam tuned to 250 lumens at 5000K — the color temperature where PCB silkscreen reads best — with no spot mode to fumble through. One button cycles high/medium/low/red; hold for off. It does the PC job perfectly because it was designed for exactly one job.

demo.program:
print("Fixed flood, 250 lm, 5000K (silkscreen reads best at this temp).")
print("No spot mode to fumble through. Button: high/med/low/red, hold=off.")
print("Designed for exactly one job: seeing inside PCs.")

t: Signature Weight Balance: The Rear-Cell Design
title: Signature Weight Balance: The Rear-Cell Design
description: The Signature lamp puts the cell in a rear pod, balancing the front LED so the lamp does not nose-dive during long sessions. Total 2.4 ounces, balanced front-to-back. The strap is wide, soft, and silicone-lined so it grips without pinching — it stays put when you lean into a case. Balance is the comfort feature nobody lists and everybody feels.

demo.program:
print("Rear cell pod: balances LED, no nose-dive. 2.4 oz total.")
print("Wide soft silicone-lined strap: grips, doesn't pinch, stays on leaning in.")
print("Balance: the comfort feature nobody lists, everybody feels.")

title: Signature Tilt Detents
description: The Signature tilt hinge has five positive detents — level, down 30, down 60, straight down, and up — each clicking firmly into place. Down-60 is the header-reading angle; straight-down is the board-scan angle. The detents hold through thousands of adjustments because they are metal-on-metal, not plastic friction that wears smooth.

demo.program:
print("5 detents: level, -30, -60 (headers), -90 (board scan), up.")
print("Metal-on-metal: holds through 1000s of adjustments (plastic wears smooth).")
print("Click to the angle: repeatable lighting, every time.")

title: Signature Dock: Always Charged
description: The Signature dock is a weighted bench stand with USB-C: the lamp drops in lens-up after every session and charges. A green LED means ready. The dock's weight means one-handed docking. The discipline of 'dock after session' works because the dock is right there on the bench — charging happens by habit, not by reminder.

print("Weighted USB-C dock: drop in lens-up, green = ready.")
print("One-handed docking. Dock on bench = charging by habit, not reminder.")
print("'Dock after session' works because the dock is RIGHT THERE.")

It is in the normal cycle (not a hidden long-press), because late-night builders actually use it. Red is a first-class mode, not an afterthought.

title: Signature vs Standard Headlamps
description: A standard headlamp is a general outdoor light with modes you will never use and a spot beam wrong for cases. The Signature is a case-tuned flood at the right color temperature, balanced, with detent tilt and a bench dock. Same LEDs, different priorities — the Signature spends its design budget on the PC job instead of the hiking job.

t: Signature Strap System: Bench and Hard-Hat
title: Signature Strap System: Bench and Hard-Hat

title: Signature Battery Standard: USB-C Only
description: The Signature lamp charges only via USB-C — no proprietary cradles, no weird cells. Any phone charger, power bank, or bench USB port charges it. In the field, the same power bank that charges the phone charges the lamp. Proprietary charging is a tax on forgetfulness; USB-C is infrastructure you already own.

print("USB-C only: phone charger, power bank, bench port - all work.")
print("Field: same power bank charges phone + lamp.")
print("Proprietary charging = tax on forgetfulness. USB-C = owned infrastructure.")

title: Signature Low-Battery Behavior
description: The Signature lamp steps down gracefully: at 20 percent it drops to medium with a slow blink warning, at 10 percent to low — never a sudden blackout mid-procedure. The step-down is documented on the dock card so it never surprises. A lamp that dies suddenly during an EPS connection is a lamp that gets thrown; this one never does.

demo.program:
print("20%: step to medium + slow blink. 10%: step to low. Never sudden blackout.")
print("Documented on dock card: never a surprise.")
print("Graceful step-down > sudden darkness mid-procedure.")

title: Signature Lens and Beam Maintenance
description: The lens wipes with the included microfiber (in the dock base); the flood diffuser pops off for washing when dusty. Check the tilt detents yearly — they are metal and rated for the lamp's life, but grit kills any hinge. The strap washes monthly. Ten minutes a year keeps the beam like new.

print("Yearly: detent check (metal, lifetime-rated, but grit kills hinges).")
print("Monthly: strap wash. 10 min/year keeps the beam like new.")

title: Signature Training: The Dark-Case Drill
description: New builders drill in a dark room: open a case, connect front-panel headers, route one cable — headlamp only, timed. Under ten minutes with all headers correct passes. The drill teaches beam aiming, detent angles, and working by flood alone. Anyone who passes never fears a dark case again.

description: Shops keep one charged spare Signature lamp on the dock — when a builder's lamp dies mid-job (it happens despite docks), the spare swaps in seconds and the dead one takes the dock. title: Signature Beam Check Card
description: The dock card includes a beam check: shine at the card's test pattern from arm's length — the flood should be even edge to edge, the 5000K white neutral. Unevenness means a dirty diffuser (wash it); yellowing means LED aging (note it, plan replacement). A thirty-second check that keeps the light honest.

demo.program:
print("Card test pattern at arm's length: flood even edge-to-edge, neutral white.")
print("Uneven = wash diffuser. Yellowing = LED aging (plan replacement).")
print("30 seconds keeps the light honest.")

title: The Complete Signature Lighting Discipline
description: The full Signature lighting discipline: lamp on before the case opens, detent aimed per task, brightness matched, red for nights, docked after every session, pre-close scan every build, dark-case drill for newcomers, spare on the shop dock. Seeing is the first step of doing — the discipline makes sure the seeing never fails.

demo.program:
disc = ["lamp on before open", "detent aimed per task", "brightness matched",
        "red for nights", "docked after session", "pre-close scan",
        "dark-case drill", "shop spare on dock"]
for i, d in enumerate(disc, 1):
    print(f"  {i}. {d}")
print("Seeing is the first step of doing. Make sure seeing never fails.")
